assessment.overall_rationale: The two module sets are near-mirror decompositions of the same P21 program (biosynthetic enzymes, SREBP2 sterol-sensing feedback, and VLDL/acetyl-CoA lipid coupling), so the strongest signal lies on the diagonal (1-1, 2-2, 3-3) with off-diagonal pairs showing only partial or contextual overlap due to shared broad hepatic cholesterol/lipid domain rather than shared core mechanism.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe the identical complete mevalonate-to-cholesterol enzymatic cascade in hepatocytes with near-total gene overlap and the same mechanistic ordering.
Both concern cholesterol biosynthesis, but L1 is the enzymatic pathway itself while R2 is the SCAP/INSIG1/SREBP2 transcriptional control layer over that pathway, a different central mechanism.
Only the shared mention of Acss2 supplying acetyl-CoA links the pure biosynthetic enzyme cascade to R3's acetyl-CoA/VLDL coupling narrative, which is peripheral to L1's core.

L2's SCAP/INSIG1/SREBP2 regulatory feedback controls the same broad cholesterol biosynthesis process as R1, but R1's content is the enzymatic pathway itself, not the sensing/transcriptional mechanism.
Both center on the same SCAP-INSIG1-SREBP2-Ldlr sterol-sensing feedback mechanism with identical regulators; R2 adds a refinement identifying Erg28 and Rdh11 as direct SREBP2 targets.
L2's sterol-sensing transcriptional feedback and R3's acetyl-CoA/VLDL export coupling involve distinct regulators and mechanisms, sharing only the general hepatic lipid/cholesterol domain.
L3's VLDL-TG assembly/export regulators (Dgat2, Mttp) have no mechanistic role in R1's pure cholesterol biosynthesis enzyme cascade beyond general pathway coupling.
L3's VLDL export regulators (Dgat2, Mttp) are mechanistically distinct from R2's SREBP2 sterol-sensing transcriptional control, sharing only broad hepatic cholesterol context.

Both modules center on the same Dgat2/Mttp/Acss2 regulator set coupling VLDL-lipid export to cholesterol synthesis; R3 refines this with MASLD/HCC disease context and ACLY-independent acetyl-CoA detail.
